utility.value: Xcel Energy (Public Service Company of Colorado)
utility.notes: Xcel Energy's Colorado Communities Served list (10/2015) shows Englewood with gas and electricity service. The City's Solar Energy Resources page cites Xcel Energy Community Energy Reports (2022) for the City of Englewood. No City source states that every Englewood address is served by Xcel Energy, so check the utility named on your electric bill before you apply for interconnection.

value.name: Xcel Energy
value.notes: Applies to addresses served by Xcel Energy. Check the utility named on your electric bill.

county.notes: The City's Homeowner Affidavit refers to current Arapahoe County records for the property, and its building fee schedule lists an Arapahoe County Open Space Tax.

permit_authority.value: City of Englewood Building and Codes Division
permit_authority.notes: The Building and Codes Division is part of the City's Community Development Department. The City says solar PV systems in Englewood require review, approval, and issuance of a building permit, and approval of the required inspections. The U.S. Postal Service gives Englewood mailing addresses to some areas in Sheridan, Greenwood Village, Centennial, Cherry Hills Village, unincorporated Arapahoe County and unincorporated Douglas County. The City says zip codes 80110 and 80113 cover the City of Englewood, the City of Sheridan and the City of Cherry Hills Village, and 80111 and 80112 cover unincorporated Arapahoe and Douglas counties, Cherry Hills Village, Greenwood Village and Centennial. For building questions about an address in those zip codes, the City says to contact the right jurisdiction; the City of Englewood is at 303.762.2300. To check whether an address is inside the City of Englewood, the City points to its Street Guide or the Colorado Sales and Use Tax lookup. The City commits to processing small rooftop solar PV permit applications in a turnaround time of 5 business days. The page counts business days and does not define a small rooftop system. This is a commitment listed on the City's Solar Energy Resources page as part of its work toward SolSmart designation.

permit_url.notes: The City's Plan Submittal Requirements page covers commercial, residential, demolition and solar projects. Create a secure account at ims.englewoodco.gov to submit required documents, receive notifications, make online payments and communicate with staff. All permits and licenses must be submitted through the online portal at ims.englewoodco.gov, and hardcopy solar submittals will not be accepted. The City says it uses an online solar specific permit application.

interconnection_url.notes: For Xcel Energy customers. Xcel says that in most cases the developer or installer submits the interconnection application on your behalf, or you can manage your own. Xcel highly recommends that construction of your system should not commence until your application receives full approval from the Xcel Energy engineering team and all final agreements are fully signed. After submission, Xcel does a technical review and, if needed, a detailed engineering study, and provides an interconnection agreement. Xcel says the interconnection work ends with a permission to operate letter from Xcel to the generator owner. Xcel's permission to operate is separate from the City permit and the City's inspections.

value.name: Renewable Battery Connect
value.description: Xcel says that when you add an eligible solar charged battery to your home or small business and participate, you let Xcel automatically manage your battery during periods of peak demand on the grid. Upfront incentive, General: $250 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to $5,000 per application). Income Qualified: $1,000 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). Disproportionately Impacted Community: $500 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). There is also a $100 annual participation incentive for all customer types for participating in control events (for 5 years).
value.eligibility: An Xcel Energy program for a home or small business that adds an eligible solar charged battery. Xcel says eligible solar battery equipment includes all Tesla Powerwall models or all current Enphase models. Check that Xcel is your electric utility first.

battery_programs.notes: Amounts are from Xcel's Renewable Battery Connect page, which shows a 2026 General incentive budget with budget available, on figures dated 11/02/2026.

value.required_when: For each roof slope with solar PV panels, a 36 inch pathway from the lowest edge of the roof to the ridge is required on the same roof slope, on an adjacent roof slope, or straddling the same and adjacent roof slopes. Detached carports, shade structures and detached garages are exempt from the pathways and ridge setbacks.

required_documents.notes: From the City's Plan Submittal Requirements: Solar Photovoltaic (PV) handout. Drawings must be submitted in PDF format and in black and white, and all documents must be unlocked, scaled and full-size. The online system requires you to combine certain documents into a single file, so follow the upload screen. Failure to comply with these minimal standards will result in a rejection of your project. An earlier City checklist for solar PV (Revised 07/2023) asks for a site observation letter for the roof cavity that indicates the adequacy of the roof and all retrofits as needed. That checklist lists the 2021 International Residential Code, and the City's 2026 Building Permit Fee Schedule still prints "2021 International Code Effective July 31, 2023" in its header, while the City's Building & Codes page and its Construction & Design Criteria sheet list the 2024 International Residential Code. Confirm with the Building and Codes Division which code edition to note on your plans. The City's Construction & Design Criteria sheet lists the 2023 National Electrical Code and gives a ground snow load of 30 PSF and a wind speed of 107 Vmph (138 Vult) for Risk Category 2.

value: Create an account at ims.englewoodco.gov and submit the solar permit application and plans online. Hardcopy submittals will not be accepted.
Wait for the permit: a permit application is not the approval to begin work. Post the permit near the front of the property, visible from the street.

Request each inspection online at ims.englewoodco.gov, or with the City's fillable form if you cannot use iMS. The owner (if the homeowner applied for the permit) or the contractor requests inspections in advance.
If you ask, the City offers inspection appointment times for solar projects instead of appointment windows.
Before you begin each new phase, all required inspections for the work just completed must show "approved" or "partial inspection only" in iMS.

Xcel Energy customers: after Xcel's approval and signed agreements, Xcel works with you and your contractors to witness test and energize the system, and issues a permission to operate letter to the generator owner.
inspection_steps.notes: The City's solar page says residential solar permits have a minimum of two inspections per permit and an average inspection timeline of 24 hours. The City's solar page says residential solar permits get at least two inspections but does not name them, so ask the Building and Codes Division which inspections to request. Indoor inspections will not be performed if an adult is not present. The Inspections page says weekend, after hours or holiday inspections are not available, while the 2026 fee schedule lists inspections outside of normal business hours at $75 per hour (minimum charge = 2 hours). Confirm with the Building and Codes Division before you plan an inspection outside 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday through Friday. Passing the City's inspections is not Xcel Energy's permission to operate.

value.program_or_pathway: Solar PV building permit, applied for online at ims.englewoodco.gov
other_conditions: A Contractor License or Certificate of Registration is required to perform construction work within the Englewood city limits.

Electrical contractors need an R-1 Certificate of Registration (no fee), which requires a City of Englewood license registered at ims.englewoodco.gov, a State of Colorado Master License and a State of Colorado Contractor License. Licenses and certificates expire one year from the date of issuance.
If a roof retrofit is required, a Class C (or better) general contractor must install the additional support members and is added to the solar permit as a sub-contractor.

A homeowner who does the work needs a Homeowner Affidavit in addition to the permit. The property must be in the homeowner's name and be their primary residence based upon current Arapahoe County records. The affidavit lists Electrical among the areas of responsibility a homeowner permit can cover.

Homeowner permits are not allowed for commercial, investment or rental properties, flips, new construction or similar, unless the property owner holds an ICC Class C contractor's certificate or better and is a registered general contractor with the City. Anyone hired, or anyone outside the immediate family who helps, must obtain a contractor's license from the City for their scope of work.

The City recognizes solar PV systems as a general accessory use in all zone districts (Englewood Municipal Code 16-4-4). For systems attached to the primary structure, setback and height standards are in EMC Title 16, Table 5-2 for residential lots.
Xcel Energy net metering: you must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer, and the name on the application must match the name on the Xcel Energy account or bill.

Xcel Energy net metering: expected generation, combined with other distributed generation serving the service address, must not exceed 200% of historical consumption (the previous 12 months at the time of application submission).
Xcel Energy net metering: all equipment must be UL 1741 SB certified and listed within the Solar Equipment Lists on the California Energy Commission website.

eligibility_constraints.notes: License, homeowner and zoning conditions are the City's. Size, equipment and account conditions are Xcel Energy's and apply to Xcel customers.

value.notes: From the Building Permit Fee Schedule effective January 1, 2026.

permit_fees.notes: From the City's Building Permit Fee Schedule, effective January 1, 2026, which sets building permit fees by total valuation. The schedule lists no fee specific to solar permits. For a valuation of $2,001 to $25,000, the fee is $78.92 for the first $2,000 plus $15.95 for each additional $1,000 or fraction thereof. For $25,001 to $50,000, it is $445.87 for the first $25,000 plus $11.51 for each additional $1,000 or fraction thereof. For $50,001 to $100,000, it is $733.62 for the first $50,000 plus $7.97 for each additional $1,000 or fraction thereof. Plan review is 65% of the building permit fee, and the 65% plan review fee is waived for single-family, owner occupied dwellings. Use tax is 3.8% on one-half the total valuation, and the Arapahoe County Open Space Tax is .25% on one-half the total valuation. The fee schedule lists re-inspection at $100 per hour, while the City's Inspections page says a reinspection fee of $75 could be charged. Confirm the current amount with the Building and Codes Division. The schedule notes that other fees may be charged by planning and zoning, engineering and utilities.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Income Qualified upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says customers who qualify under the terms of Income Qualified can receive an upfront rebate of $3 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer and qualify under Xcel's Income Qualified terms.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Disproportionately Impacted Communities upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says Disproportionately Impacted Communities can receive an upfront rebate of $0.50 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer. The rebate is for Disproportionately Impacted Communities.

rebates.notes: These are Xcel Energy programs for Xcel customers. Xcel's page says that as of 10/05/2026 it moved $1,050,000 from Solar*Rewards C&I to the Solar*Rewards Residential IQ/DIC program. The City's solar page says residents who meet income eligibility requirements may be able to secure free solar via GRID Alternatives' Energy for All program. The City's solar page describes no City cash rebate for residential solar.
